purpose: Machine-checkable bridge contracts between the three verification projects of this repository. Main project uses Lean 4.34.0 (no Mathlib); local-field and bridge use Lean 4.34.0-rc2 (Mathlib). A proof cannot be imported across those toolchains, so a main-to-bridge edge is NOT a kernel-checked dependency: it is an audited contract, pinned by elaborated statement text and vendored definition types. The local-field-to-bridge edge is a real Lean import and needs no contract.

normalisation.note: Whitespace is collapsed after prefix stripping. Equality of the remaining text is a property of the two elaborated types, not of the source files.

contracts.claim: The abstract discrete scale model composes multiplicatively. On actual Q_p the multiplicative coordinate is the norm scale factor, and the additive coordinate is the valuation; both are proved to have exactly the predicted composition law, and iterated rescaling telescopes to the sum of exponents.
contracts.notes: The model uses Nat scales; the arithmetic statement uses Int exponents. This is an instantiation, not a statement identity: the model's product of scales corresponds to the sum of valuation exponents.

contracts.claim: The abstract model proves that a scale is determined by its value on the unit. On actual Q_p the corresponding statement is that the value at 1 determines the automorphism, hence determines exactly one lattice layer of the ball image: the joint data is a graph.
contracts.notes: Uniqueness of the layer index is what converts the abstract normalisation statement into the non-rectangularity obstruction of BR-03/BR-04.

contracts.claim: The rectangularity interface (LeftAllowed, RightAllowed, IsRectangular) and the equivalence 'rectangular iff the joint relation is the product of its marginals' are carried over to the second toolchain: the elaborated statements agree after namespace normalisation, the elaborated types of the three vendored definitions agree, and their definition-body source text is checked for identity by the auditor. This is an interface-identity audit, NOT a kernel-level proof transfer and NOT a claim of semantic equivalence across toolchains.
contracts.notes: Comparing elaborated types alone cannot distinguish two predicates with the same type but different bodies, so the auditor also compares definition-body source text. Cross-toolchain kernel comparison is impossible here because the two projects use different Lean versions.

contracts.claim: The abstract Boolean counterexample showing that separate kappa- and sigma-admissibility does not entail joint admissibility is realized on actual arithmetic data: automorphisms of Q_p versus integer layers of the unit ball. Both marginals are total and the relation is not rectangular, because the relation is a graph over an infinite ladder. A general graph obstruction is isolated, and the normalised sub-relation is proved rectangular, so the failure is exactly the rescaling freedom.
contracts.notes: Still a base-field statement. It does not assert that any Step (v) objection is correct or incorrect.

contracts.claim: In the base field the ladder is strictly *antitone* — a larger index is a smaller ball, so `k ≤ m` gives `layer m ⊆ layer k` and widening goes towards smaller indices. Moving from `layer k` to `layer m` is realised by the single dilation of signed exponent `m - k`. This is an identity between sets of p-adic numbers; it defines no measure, no volume, no log-volume and no optimal price, and must not be read as a quantitative cost formula.
contracts.notes: The repository records that enlarging a container is only a repair if the added volume cost still meets the target estimate. This contract supplies only the layer-move identity; the volume estimate itself is not formalised, and no cost function is defined here.

contracts.claim: Any rectangular repair freezes the lattice layer. If a sub-relation of the joint lattice relation admits independent marginal reasoning (is rectangular), then all of its admissible pairs share one layer: independent marginal reasoning is available only after the rescaling freedom has been given up. This converts the BR-04 obstruction from a counterexample into a design constraint on any repair attempt.
contracts.notes: Base-field lattice statement. It constrains what a repair may assume, and says nothing about whether the actual IUT Step (v) objection is correct.

contracts.claim: The integer slot model of the label action is realized on actual p-adic tuples. Relabelling by a permutation conjugates a slotwise scalar family, so a slotwise action is sigma-equivariant exactly when the family is sigma-invariant; it moves components but preserves each component's valuation data. The main project's swap23 model is a generic-type reindexing with no scalar action, so the conjugation statement is new to this toolchain.
contracts.notes: Slot set is an abstract Fin n with an explicit permutation, not the slot set of a real Hodge theater. The result answers only the toy form of the round-5 question on label-independent synchronization.

contracts.claim: The abstract integer weighted comparison is realized as an actual weighted valuation ledger on p-adic tuples. The ledger shifts by exactly the weighted sum of scalar valuations, the norm product is its exponential, and the ledger is invariant under a label action for every tuple if and only if the weight vector is invariant under that action. The pilot-style weights (1,1,2,1) therefore fail invariance under the swap 2<->3, with a concrete witnessing tuple, while the unweighted total is invariant under every label action.
not_constructed: pilot weight realisation from real theta data
contracts.notes: The weights are arbitrary integers chosen by hand; the pilot pattern (1,1,2,1) is used only as a concrete non-uniform example. No claim is made that it is the weight vector of the real pilot.
